patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of persistent fatigue and several episodes of lower abdominal pain. Despite being on sick leave for 2 weeks, symptoms have not improved. She expresses a concern that she might have cancer and requests a diagnostic laparoscopy. She was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months prior, currently taking omeprazole.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Works as a nurse, has been under a lot of stress at work.

Review_of_Systems.Skin: Numerous crusts along the left arm veins
Review_of_Systems.Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur along the right-upper sternal border
Review_of_Systems.Musculoskeletal: Generalized weakness of the proximal muscles

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with fatigue, episodes of lower abdominal pain, and a self-stated high cancer concern.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today—what brings you in? Patient: For about two months I’ve had persistent fatigue and I’ve had a few episodes of lower abdominal pain. I’ve been on sick leave for two weeks, but I’m not improving, and I’m very worried it could be something like cancer.
[ASK] Have you had a persistent cough with shortness of breath that worsens over time (especially with exertion or smoking exposure)?

Patient: No, I haven’t had a persistent cough or shortness of breath, and I don’t recall any worsening with exertion or any smoking-related exposure. I’m mainly feeling persistent fatigue, pale with generalized weakness, and occasional lower abdominal pain.
[ASK] Have you experienced progressive memory/behavior changes (e.g., personality or language changes) over months to years?

No, I haven’t noticed any progressive memory or behavior changes, or changes in my personality or speech. I’m mainly dealing with ongoing fatigue, paleness and generalized proximal weakness, plus those occasional lower abdominal pain episodes.

Patient: No, I haven’t been told I have CLL, and I don’t know of any swollen lymph nodes or similar diagnoses—my main issues are persistent fatigue with paleness and generalized weakness, plus a few episodes of lower abdominal pain.

Patient: I don’t have any known kidney disease, and I haven’t noticed swelling in my legs, reduced urine, or foamy urine—my symptoms are mainly fatigue, paleness with generalized weakness, and occasional lower abdominal pain.

Patient: I was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease about six months ago and I’ve been taking omeprazole since then; I’m not having new burning in my upper abdomen, but I still have persistent fatigue, pale appearance, generalized weakness, and occasional lower abdominal pain.

Patient: No, I haven’t had symptoms like persistent upper abdominal/back pain, jaundice, or unexplained weight loss—my main ongoing problems are persistent fatigue with paleness and generalized proximal weakness, plus a few episodes of lower abdominal pain. I’m mostly worried about something serious because I’m not improving despite time off work.
[DDX] Brief Psychotic Disorder  , Chronic kidney failure, Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), Factitious disorder, Gastric peptic ulcer
